title: TTM Category A: Roadway Foundations & Safety
description: Fundamental road reserve hazard mitigation, pedestrian containment, and personal protective equipment standards aligned with CoPTTM and NZGTTM operational guidelines.

questions.prompt: What is the primary objective of a Temporary Traffic Management (TTM) safety zone?
options: To completely eliminate all traffic congestion on arterial routes
To separate live traffic from workers, plant, and road users safely
To maximize the speed of heavy transport through active work areas
To minimize the need for high-visibility PPE
questions.explanation: Safety zones exist primarily to create positive physical and visual separation between live traffic corridors and on-foot workers or plant.

questions.prompt: Under standard New Zealand guidelines, what is the mandatory high-visibility garment standard for daytime work on dynamic road reserves?
options: Standard Level 1 / TTMC-W17 compliant day/night garment
Any fluorescent t-shirt without retroreflective banding
Standard black wet-weather jacket
General high-vis vest without long tail protection
questions.explanation: TTMC-W17 compliant garments ensure adequate visual surface area and retroreflective performance across all lighting conditions.

questions.prompt: When establishing a pedestrian detour around an obstructed footway, what is the key safety requirement?
options: Direct pedestrians into live traffic lanes with cones only
Provide continuous physical protection, ramps for accessibility, and clear signage
Advise pedestrians to find an alternative route across unpaved terrain
Close the footpath without providing an alternate corridor
questions.explanation: Pedestrian detours must maintain universal accessibility, trip hazard protection, and continuous physical barriers separating them from vehicular traffic.

title: TTM Category B: High-Speed Corridors & Expressways
description: Advanced protocols for operating in environments exceeding 70 km/h, focusing on advance warning tapers, crash cushion attenuation, and lateral buffer management.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum recommended longitudinal buffer space in a permanent 100 km/h posted speed environment?
options: 10 meters
25 meters
50 meters or greater as specified in the approved TMP
Zero meters if an attenuator truck is stationed upstream
questions.explanation: Longitudinal buffer zones provide critical stopping and recovery distance for errant vehicles before entering the active work space.

questions.prompt: What operational function does a Truck Mounted Attenuator (TMA) serve when positioned upstream?
options: Primary mobile canteen for site workers
Energy absorption vehicle designed to protect workers from high-speed rear impacts
Storage for extra traffic cones and sandbags
Speed enforcement camera platform
questions.explanation: TMAs are crash-tested safety devices designed to absorb kinetic energy and redirect errant vehicles away from workers on foot.

questions.prompt: When is a Dynamic Advance Warning sign required on high-speed expressway tapers?
options: Only during severe weather events
At all times when visibility is obstructed or high-speed lane shifts are implemented
Never, standard static signs are always sufficient
Only when operating between midnight and 4:00 AM
questions.explanation: Dynamic variable message signage gives high-speed drivers early warning to decelerate and merge before encountering lane restrictions.

title: TTM Category C: Mobile Operations & TMP Auditing
description: Continuous mobile closures, tail-car spacing, shadow vehicle positioning, and compliance audit verification under operational risk management guidelines.

questions.prompt: In a continuous mobile operation (e.g. line marking or road sweeping), what is the function of the Shadow Vehicle?
options: To transport extra fuel and tools
To track behind the lead work vehicle, warning approaching traffic and providing rear protection
To enforce parking restrictions along urban curbs
To test road surface temperature
questions.explanation: Shadow vehicles maintain a calculated trailing distance equipped with TMA and flashing arrow boards to shield the lead maintenance plant.

questions.prompt: What is the consequence of failing a critical site safety audit by an authorized RCA Auditor?
options: A small verbal reminder with no logging
Immediate issuance of a Notice to Correct or Site Stop Work directive
Automatic extension of the working window
Immediate refund of permit application fees
questions.explanation: Critical non-compliance (such as missing tapers or unapproved lane closures) can result in an immediate Stop Work Order by the Road Controlling Authority.

questions.prompt: How frequently must on-site TTM audits and hazard checks be documented during an active shift?
options: Once at the start of the week
At regular intervals throughout the shift and whenever site or weather conditions change
Only when an incident occurs
No documentation is needed once set up
questions.explanation: Active sites require ongoing monitoring and logbook documentation at regular intervals (e.g., every 2 hours) to record changing traffic and environmental factors.
